title: doftiles
description: personal dotfiles as a GNU stow repository: one package per directory, installed into your user directory with a single command; herbstluftwm as the window manager, on-deploy as the installer.

content.heading: doftiles - the stow packages
content: **doftiles** is the dotfiles repository: every top-level directory is a **GNU stow package** whose contents mirror $HOME.
installing a package stows its tree over your user directory as symlinks - the files stay in the repository, your home only ever holds links.
[https://github.com/akinevz2/doftiles](https://github.com/akinevz2/doftiles)

content.heading: the system it moves into
content: the session stack is **herbstluftwm** as a systemd user unit, a compositor and a notification daemon beside it - all user units, no display manager required.
on the WSL2 hosts the display is a Windows-side X server: a probe unit runs first, resolves the display and exports it to the systemd user manager, and every WM-side unit requires it.
the same repository deploys onto bare-metal and container targets - the manifests decide what a given machine gets.

content.heading: the packages
content: **herbstluftwm** - the window manager stack: the autostart, the theme, the float/focus machinery, the rofi menus and command palette, all systemd user units.
**polybar** - the bar: config, module scripts and control tooling; the polyframes module execs the **polyframes** binary directly.
**shell** - the shell rc files, the credentials plumbing and the small user tools.
**dunst** - the notification daemon config and unit.
**wsl** - the WSL-interop pieces: the runtime-conditional browser wrapper and the env fragment; machines opt in per host.
**agents** - the opencode and poolside configuration, screencast plugin included.
**on-deploy**, **herbctl**, **herbstutil**, **polyframes** - each submodule is its own stow package; its build artifact lands inside the package and stow ships it.
a handful of service packages (novnc, xvfb, x11vnc, xrdp) deploy individually, on purpose - the generic build ships none of them.

content.heading: how deployment works
content: files put under a named package can be installed to your user directory with a single command.
changes and updates propagate content to your user directory automatically inside the linked files - edit the repository file and the change is live, because the link points at it.
removing a whole package of configuration files is a single command: the links go, and your real files were never touched.
what a machine gets is declared up front: package lists, required binaries, submodule pins and user units - one manifest file each. personalize a manifest per host and pulls stay merge-clean.

content.heading: the recipes
content: `make install` - the full deploy: build the installer, stow the packages, apply the recorded config, report status.
`make bootstrap` - a fresh machine: submodule checkouts, toolchain bootstrap and the build/install walk for every submodule artifact.
`make update` - the safe pull: fetch, fast-forward, materialize the pinned submodules. `make update install` runs the install step exactly once.
`make stow-<pkg>` / `make unstow-<pkg>` - one package in or out.
`make status` - the health check: installer, services, credentials reminder.
the whole chain is headless-friendly with `YES=1`; anything needing root asks through an interactive terminal instead of hanging.

content.heading: quirks
content: hooks needing a running WM are guarded and no-op with a note on headless targets.
the service units needing X stay enabled-but-failed until X exists - on WSL2 that is the Windows-side server.
the deploy target is machine-local state; a fresh host starts generic and personalizes from there.

content.heading: stable in v1.0.0
content: the deployment scope is defined by four manifests - stows.depends, wm.depends, system.depends, services.depends, one file each - no per-package code, no hardcoded paths; the manifests decide what gets deployed, the per-package makefiles decide how.
the display is resolved in exactly one place: the probe unit runs first and exports it to the systemd user manager; every WM-side unit requires it.
the install step is one chain - configure, preserve, packages install, status.
`make update` never rebuilds what it does not need to; a fresh submodule pin lands its binary through the unconditional rebuild.

content.heading: examples
content: the whole system deploys from one repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/akinevz2/doftiles ~/dots
cd ~/dots
make bootstrap    # submodules, toolchains, artifact walk
make toolchain    # the toolchains the packages build with
make install      # stow the packages, apply the recorded config
```
updating is two recipes:

```sh
make update          # fetch, fast-forward, materialize the pins
make update install  # ...and run the install step exactly once
```
the full walkthrough (headless runs, the update path) is a separate post: [try it out](/blog/releases/try_it_out).
